about: Labels for runs recorded before daq.py (runs 001-068). category: test (key experiment), partial (heated, incomplete or tripped), setup (commissioning/sensor checks), failure (dead cartridge), idle (no heating). map: which raw data column (amplifier) is TC1 heater side, TC2 barrier rear, TC3. All heated runs had amplifier 2 on the heater side.

006.title: First heat: mica only, leaned on block
006.setup: 1 mica sheet; heater-side TC wired beside the cartridge, rear TC wired to the far face; leaned against the cinder block (no sand). Variac voltage not recorded. McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC).
006.review: Heater driven by hand from the variac (no relay control yet). Hotter TC peaked 261 °C at 1:18; the other 220 °C at 1:28, so one mica layer barely slowed the heat. Which raw channel was on the heater side is not recorded: assumed raw 2, which is hotter and leads, as in every later run. About 60 fault rows per channel.

009.title: First relay control attempt (EXP2, 30 V)
009.review: EXP2 started; within 4.5 s raw TC2 jumped past the 140 °C rear limit and tripped. Raw TC2 was on the heater side, i.e. the probes were already the other way round from the plan. Garbage frames (2047.75 °C) follow.

011.title: Control check with one TC (heat gun)
011.review: Single-thermocouple check of the EXP2 hold-at-300 °C logic while TC2 was unplugged; the operator had planned to test it with a heat gun. TC1 jumped 156 → 302 °C in 5 s, too fast for the cartridge. Not a barrier test.

017.title: Test 1: 1 mica / 2 basalt / 1 Al, rear cutoff 85 °C
017.setup: 1 mica (85165K26, 0.032 in) / 2 basalt fabric (3/64 in) / 1 aluminum sheet. Semi-gravelly sand. McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC). Variac voltage not recorded (30 V preset in config).
017.result: Heater side reached 86 °C; rear cutoff (85 °C, wrongly on the heater-side channel) stopped it.
017.review: Operator: "first successful run". EXP2 hold-at-300 °C program, but the probes were swapped relative to the software, so the 85 °C rear cutoff watched the heater side and ended heating at 3:10 with the heater side at 85.75 °C. The rear rose only 5 °C. Useful as a working end-to-end check, not as barrier data.

019.title: EXP3 short start/stop
019.setup: 1 mica / 2 basalt / 1 Al, semi-gravelly sand. Variac preset 65 V.
019.review: Brief EXP3 starts used to check that stop cuts the heat. 019: heater on 32 s, heater side coasted to 113.5 °C after stop. 021: 5 s, no response in the data.

021.title: EXP3 short start/stop

021.review: Brief EXP3 starts used to check that stop cuts the heat. 019: heater on 32 s, heater side coasted to 113.5 °C after stop. 021: 5 s, no response in the data.

023.title: Test 2: hold 300 °C, ~70 V, 1 mica / 2 basalt / 1 Al
023.setup: 1 mica / 2 basalt fabric / 1 aluminum. Semi-gravelly sand. McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC) at about 70 V (operator; 65 V preset).
023.result: Held near 300 °C for 20 min; rear reached 84 °C and was still rising.
023.review: Operator: "great", "successful". EXP3 held the heater side at 300 °C (on/off with prediction): 299.0 ± 2.4 °C, range 294.5–303 °C, for about 20 minutes. Reached 100 °C at 0:32 and 200 °C at 1:14, then held for about 20 minutes (stopped at 1,218 s of a planned 1,800 s hold). The rear climbed steadily to 83.75 °C and had not levelled off when the run was stopped, so this barrier does not keep the rear under 85 °C for 30 min at 300 °C. Fitted rear gain 0.21 (±0.7 °C).

026.title: Test 3: EXP4 to 700 °C, rear cutoff 85 °C
026.setup: Barrier not recorded (probably the 1 mica / 2 basalt / 1 Al stack still in place). Semi-gravelly sand. McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC), 100 V preset.
026.result: Heater side 707 °C; rear hit its 85 °C cutoff at 9:18, peaked 110.5 °C four minutes after heat off.
026.review: Operator: "it went fine". 100 °C hold, NEXT, 90 s ramp to 200 °C, full power to 700 °C, then hold. 700 °C reached 6:10 after heat start. The 85 °C rear cutoff tripped at 9:18 and the rear kept rising for 4 more minutes to 110.5 °C: the barrier releases stored heat long after the heater stops. Fitted rear gain 0.21.

028.title: Test 4: EXP5 700 °C, 60 s hold (completed)
028.setup: Barrier not recorded (same session as 030/033). Semi-gravelly sand. McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC), 100 V preset.
028.result: Completed: 700 °C at 4:28, 60 s hold, heat off. Heater peak 708 °C, rear peak 83.5 °C at 11:52.
028.review: Operator: "it went well". The cleanest full profile: 100 °C hold, NEXT, ramp to 200 °C, full power to 700 °C (reached 4:28 after heat start), 60 s hold, heat off. Rear peaked 83.5 °C 7 minutes after the heater-side peak. Fitted rear gain 0.20. Reference run for the old 300 W cartridge at 100 V.

030.title: EXP5 repeat: rear cutoff 120 °C tripped
030.setup: Barrier not recorded. Semi-gravelly sand. McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC), 100 V preset.
030.review: Same program as 028, run straight after. The rear rose much faster (fitted rear gain 0.43 vs 0.20) and tripped the 120 °C cutoff at 3:38 with the heater side only at 483 °C. Something in the stack or the rear TC's contact changed between 028 and 030; not recorded.

033.title: EXP5 repeat: rear cutoff 120 °C tripped
033.setup: Barrier not recorded. Semi-gravelly sand. McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC), 100 V preset.
033.review: Third EXP5 that afternoon. NEXT was refused for minutes by the old software's 95-105 °C window while the heater side sat at 156 °C (the operator's complaint). After the ramp, the rear tripped 120 °C at 10:10 with the heater side at 680 °C; rear peaked 153 °C. Fitted rear gain 0.28.

036.title: Test 5: 1 mica / 2 fiberglass / 1 Al, 700 °C 60 s
036.setup: 1 mica (0.032 in) / 2 fiberglass heat-barrier strip (McMaster 4234N12, 0.045 in) / 1 aluminum. Fine, less rocky sand (from run 034). McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC), 100 V preset.
036.result: 700 °C at 4:08, peak 714 °C, hold done. Rear peak 80.25 °C at 11:40 (cooldown).
036.review: EXP6 (EXP5 with NEXT allowed any time). Completed the 60 s hold at 700 °C. Heater on 176 s in total. Rear rose 55.5 °C and peaked 7.4 minutes after the heater-side peak, during cooldown. Fitted rear gain 0.20 (±1.1 °C). Compare with run 040.

038.title: EXP6 start aborted after 4 s
038.review: Started and stopped after 4 s; not a test.

040.title: Test 6: 1 mica / 3 ceramic fiber / 1 Al; cartridge died
040.setup: 1 mica (0.032 in) / 3 ceramic fiber pipe insulation (alumina, McMaster 87575K35, 1/32 in) / 1 aluminum. Fine sand. McMaster 4877K305 cartridge, 300 W at 120 V (no internal TC), 100 V preset.
040.result: 700 °C at 5:47, peak 709.5 °C, hold done; rear peak 113 °C. Cartridge failed open at the end.
040.review: Same program as 036, different barrier. Reached 700 °C 1.7 min later than 036 and needed 294 s of heating (036: 176 s), so more energy went in; the rear rose 82 °C (036: 55.5 °C). Fitted rear gain is the same as 036 (0.20), so most of the difference is the extra heat input, not the barrier. A re-heat during the hold at 18:52:48 produced no rise: the cartridge had failed (measured open circuit afterwards). Likely cause: the inside of the cartridge ran far hotter than the external TC's ~700 °C (the thermal model puts the core hundreds of degrees above the surface during fast heating), past its 760 °C rating, in sand that sheds heat poorly.

044.title: Dead cartridge: heat commanded, no rise
044.review: After run 040's cartridge failure: about 4.5 minutes of heat in total across these runs and no temperature rise. 108 V measured at the cartridge, open circuit across it. Several also show the heater-side TC reading 0.00 (wiring fault).

064.title: EXP7: internal TC on MAX31855 faulted at heat-on
064.setup: New cartridge with internal grounded K TC on amplifier 3. Control stack: 1 aluminum sheet. McMaster 8440T32 cartridge, 500 W at 120 V, internal grounded K TC.
064.review: EXP7 controlled on the cartridge's internal TC. The internal TC (grounded junction) read NaN 0.7 s after heat-on and the sensor-fault trip ended the run after 1 s. The MAX31855 needs an isolated (ungrounded) junction; this cartridge's TC is grounded to its sheath, and the readings got worse whenever the heater circuit was powered. A 47 kΩ resistor from TC− to ground did not help. Led to the TC513 approach (run 068).

068.title: EXP8: TC513 on internal TC, 650 °C; did not hold
068.setup: Barrier not recorded. McMaster 8440T32 cartridge, 500 W at 120 V, internal grounded K TC at 100 V (about 347 W). The Selec TC513 reads the internal TC with setpoint 650 °C; the DAQ relay feeds both the TC513 and the heater.
068.result: Heater side peaked 419 °C, then fell steadily to 167 °C over 10 min with the DAQ relay on. Rear peaked 110 °C.
068.review: Full power to 100 °C, cut at 0:36; the heater side kept climbing to 187 °C on stored heat. The first NEXT started the ramp, but the old ramp began its setpoint at 100 °C while the reading was ~170 °C, so nothing heated for 55 s; a second NEXT was swallowed. After 200 °C the relay stayed on (TC513 in charge). The external TC peaked 419 °C at 5:45 and then cooled exactly as with the heater off: the thermal model fits the rest of the run within 11 °C if heater power stopped for good at 5:02. So the TC513 switched the heater off once (its internal TC near 650 °C) and never switched it back on; the operator reports the TC513 was configured wrong. The 90 s hold was never started.
